o.text: Borrowed from Arabic دَاهٍ (dāhin). Compare Turkish dâhi.
From tənqidi (“critical”) + təfəkkür (“cognition, thinking”). Ultimately a calque of English critical thinking via Russian крити́ческое мышле́ние (kritíčeskoje myšlénije).

From Proto-Turkic *kïyn (“hard, difficult”).
Cognate with Kumyk qıyın, Kazakh қиын (qıyın, “difficult”), Kyrgyz кыйын (kıyın, “difficult”), Uzbek qiyin (“difficult”).
